title: An Immersed Boundary, Wall-Modeled Large-Eddy Simulation Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction of Flexible Thin Shells
content: This paper presents a numerical approach for simulating fluid-structure interaction (FSI) of flexible thin shells. Particularly, a sharp-interface immersed boundary (IB), wall-modeled large-eddy simulation (WMLES) framework is integrated with a rotation-free, large-deformation, shell element model. The proposed approach merges the advantages of wall-modeling, the IB method and the finite-element model. This enables an accurate LES of wall-bounded turbulent flows while alleviating the requirement of high near-wall resolution, and complex deformations of flexible structures in FSI can be efficiently handled on a fixed grid. In the IB-WMLES framework, two wall boundary conditions of the velocity are considered: the conventional Neumann boundary condition and a novel no-slip boundary condition, the latter of which imposes the wall stress by augmenting the eddy viscosity at the wall. The shell model is validated against standard benchmarks. The strategy of fluid-structure coupling is validated by simulating the interaction of a cantilever with the laminar flow. The present IB-FE-WMLES approach is validated by simulating the oscillation of an inverted elastic flag in the turbulent flow. The predicted results agree well with the referenced experimental data. Specially, compared to the Neumann boundary condition, the proposed no-slip boundary condition yields a result that aligns more closely with the referenced experimental data.
